lemma: L1 (reformulation of 40a). Let M range over the uniform one-pass class of 40a. (i) Logical negation: NOT(40a) <=> exists M, c, d, m0 such that for all m >= m0: S_M(m) <= s(m)^c AND tau_M(m) <= s(m)^d. Proof: negate the prefix of 40a (forall M, forall c,d, forall m0, exists m>=m0 : S>s^c or tau>s^d) by de Morgan. (ii) Eventual versus all-length bounds: if such an M has the bounds only for m >= m0, define M' that runs M for m >= m0 and, for the finitely many m < m0, uses a fixed table of answers; for each fixed m < m0 the table has constant size (it depends only on m0 and s), so S_M'(m) <= s(m)^c' and tau_M'(m) <= s(m)^d' for all m with suitable constants c', d' (absorb the constant table into the polynomial via s(m) >= m). Hence 40a is equivalent to the 'all sufficiently large m' form of the MMW hypothesis that no poly-space, poly-update-time one-pass algorithm solves exact total Search-MCSP^A[s]. Caveat for (ii): this needs s(m) >= m and the table size to be bounded by a constant independent of the machine's own s-dependence; I checked the case form only, not the uniformity conditions of [4].

proved_step: LEMMA W (exact, general n, 0<k<n). PM on K_{n,n}, row-major order, top block a = rows 1..k, bottom block b = rows k+1..n. Let F(a) = {T subset of [n], |T|=k : a admits a perfect matching of rows 1..k onto T}, g_a(b) = PM(a,b). Then F(a)=F(a') iff g_a=g_a' as functions of b. Hence the level-kn width equals the number of distinct F(a). PROOF. (1) A perfect matching of K_{n,n} splits into a matching of rows 1..k onto some T with |T|=k and a matching of rows k+1..n onto [n]\T; so g_a(b)=1 iff some T in F(a) has b matchable onto [n]\T. (2) For T, let b_T be the bottom graph whose only edges form one perfect matching of rows k+1..n onto [n]\T. Its rows can only be matched onto exactly [n]\T, so by (1) g_a(b_T)=1 iff T in F(a); hence F(a) is determined by g_a. (3) By (1), g_a(b)=1 iff some T in F(a) has b matchable onto [n]\T, a condition on the pair (F(a), b); hence g_a is determined by F(a). Together (2) and (3) give the claim. QED.

evidence: The lemma is mathematically correct: for perfect matching PM on K_{n,n} with row-major variable order, at level l=kn (after k rows), the residual function g_a(b) = PM(a,b) is in bijection with F(a) = {T subset [n], |T|=k : top k rows a admit a perfect matching onto T}. Proof: (1) Any perfect matching splits into a matching of rows 1..k onto T and rows k+1..n onto [n]\T. (2) For each T, the permutation matrix b_T matching rows k+1..n onto [n]\T satisfies g_a(b_T)=1 iff T in F(a), so F(a) is determined by g_a. (3) g_a(b)=1 iff exists T in F(a) with b matchable onto [n]\T, so g_a is determined by F(a). Hence width at level kn equals the number of distinct F(a). Verified by re-derivation; matches measured widths 8 (n=3,k=1), 16 (n=4,k=1), 37 (n=4,k=2) from cm-f8ec3fb39cab47bd. However, this width measure fails the control test (G0004): max width 4,13,59 for PM on K_{2,2}, K_{3,3}, K_{4,4} vs 2 for parity, so it is large for a function in P and cannot by itself separate the target class from P.

statement: For n>=2 and 1<=k<=n-1, let X={(i,j): i<k} and Y={(i,j): i>=k} be the edge sets of K_{n,n}. Let M[a,b]=1 iff a (subset of X) union b (subset of Y) is a perfect matching of K_{n,n}. Then rank_F(M)=C(n,k) over every field F. Closes: none. This is a control-failure lemma and does not close G0001.
derivation: (1) In a union a+b that is a perfect matching, each left vertex i<k has degree 1 in a, since b has no edges at i<k, and the right endpoints of a are distinct. So a is valid iff a is an injection f:[k]->[n]; let S(a) be its image, |S|=k. (2) Symmetrically, b is valid iff it is an injection g:{k..n-1}->[n], with image T(b) of size n-k. (3) a+b is a perfect matching iff valid(a), valid(b) and T(b)=[n]\S(a). (4) Row a depends only on S(a). Each k-set S has a nonempty row class R_S (valid a with S(a)=S), and each (n-k)-set T has a nonempty column class C_T (valid b with T(b)=T). The block R_S x C_T is all-ones if T=[n]\S and zero otherwise; invalid rows and columns are zero. (5) Distinct S give distinct T=[n]\S, so the nonzero blocks have disjoint row and column supports. M is therefore a sum of C(n,k) rank-1 blocks with disjoint supports, plus zero rows and columns, so rank_F(M)=C(n,k) over every field. (6) For k=n/2, rank >= 2^n/(n+1). Perfect matching is in P, so this rank measure fails the perfect-matching control.

proved_step:
statement_start: For every deterministic one-pass streaming machine with S state bits and a one-bit input alphabet, each transition stage can be implemented by a Boolean circuit of size O(S 2^S).
statement: Lemma (truth-table transition simulation). Let M be a deterministic one-pass machine whose configuration at each read boundary is encoded by S bits, whose next configuration after reading one input bit is a total function δ:{0,1}^S×{0,1}->{0,1}^S, and whose input length is L. There is a layered Boolean circuit with L transition layers, O(S 2^S) gates per layer, and O(S) wires carrying state between adjacent layers, whose output equals M's final configuration (and hence any Boolean output function of that configuration, if that final decoder is appended). Proof: for each output coordinate j and each pair (u,b) in {0,1}^S×{0,1} with δ(u,b)_j=1, form the minterm that is 1 exactly when the S state wires equal u and the input wire equals b. OR these minterms to obtain output coordinate j. A minterm uses O(S) literals and can be implemented with O(S) fan-in-2 gates; OR of at most 2^(S+1) minterms uses O(2^S) fan-in-2 gates per output coordinate. Summing over S coordinates gives O(S 2^S) gates per layer. Cascade the layers, feeding the initial configuration constants to the first layer and each layer's state outputs into the next; induction on layer index shows the wires equal M's configuration after each read. Appending the decoder preserves the final output. The construction is exact for all input strings of length L. This restricted lemma only gives an upper simulation bound and does not imply a lower bound for Search-MCSP or close G0001.

statement: Let L be the YES language of an exact deterministic one-pass Search-MCSP machine on inputs of fixed length N. At a cut after t bits, define the suffix residual of prefix u in {0,1}^t by L_u={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: uz in L}, and let R_t be the number of distinct such residuals. If the machine has S state bits and its final output determines membership in L, then 2^S >= R_t, hence S >= ceil(log_2 R_t).
proof: Suppose prefixes u and v reach the same state at the cut. Determinism implies that for every common suffix z, the continuation from that state produces the same final state and output on uz and vz. Exactness and the assumed membership decoder imply uz is in L iff vz is in L for every z. Therefore L_u=L_v. Distinct residuals must reach distinct machine states, so there are at least R_t states. An S-bit state has at most 2^S possibilities, giving 2^S >= R_t and the logarithmic bound.
scope: Fixed-length inputs; deterministic one-pass computation; the entire configuration relevant to future computation is included in the S-bit state; final output determines YES membership. Applies to Search-MCSP when its exact search output is decoded for validity/membership under the specified total-task convention.

statement: Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N and fix a cut after t bits. For each prefix u in {0,1}^t, define its suffix residual F_u={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: uz in F}. If R_t is the number of distinct residuals, then R_t <= min(2^t, 2^(N-t), |F|+1).
proof: There are at most 2^t prefixes and at most 2^(N-t) possible residual subsets of suffixes, giving the first two bounds. For the third, each distinct nonempty residual contains at least one suffix z. Choose one such z for each distinct nonempty residual, and choose one prefix u realizing that residual. The resulting pairs (u,z) are distinct because distinct residuals cannot be realized by the same prefix, and each pair satisfies uz in F. Thus the number of distinct nonempty residuals is at most |F|. There is at most one empty residual, so R_t <= |F|+1.
scope: Finite fixed-length Boolean language and any fixed prefix cut. For Search-MCSP the lemma applies to F equal to the YES truth tables, but supplies only an upper bound on residual width; it does not prove G0001 or an update-time lower bound.

statement: Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N, fix a cut after t bits, and put p=2^t, q=2^(N-t), k=|F|. For each prefix u define F_u={z:uz in F}, and let R_t be the number of distinct F_u. Then R_t <= min(p,q,k+1,pq-k+1).
proof: There are p rows, so R_t<=p. Each row is a subset of a q-element suffix set, so R_t<=q. For every distinct nonempty row pattern choose one matrix entry equal to 1 in a row realizing that pattern. Different patterns have different realizing rows, so the chosen entries are distinct; hence there are at most k distinct nonempty patterns, plus at most one empty pattern. Thus R_t<=k+1. For every distinct pattern other than the full pattern, choose a 0-entry in a row realizing it. Distinct patterns have distinct realizing rows, hence these chosen entries are distinct; there are pq-k zero entries. Thus there are at most pq-k non-full patterns, plus at most one full pattern, so R_t<=pq-k+1. Combining the four bounds proves the claim.

evidence: The construction is a standard DNF expansion of the transition function δ. With S state bits and 1 input bit, there are 2^{S+1} possible transitions. Each output bit is a Boolean function of S+1 variables, which can be implemented by an OR of at most 2^{S+1} minterms, each using O(S) gates. Total size O(S * 2^S) is correct.

This is a standard Myhill-Nerode style argument for deterministic one-pass streaming. If two prefixes u, v reach the same S-bit state, then for all suffixes z the machine's output on uz and vz is identical (determinism + state captures all future-relevant information). Therefore L_u = L_v. Distinct residuals require distinct states, so 2^S >= R_t. The argument is correct for the stated scope (deterministic one-pass, fixed length, state includes all configuration).

Elementary combinatorial bounds. R_t <= 2^t (number of prefixes), R_t <= 2^(N-t) (number of possible residual subsets). For R_t <= |F|+1: each distinct nonempty residual F_u contains some z with uz in F; choose one such z and the prefix u realizing it. Distinct residuals have distinct chosen u (since u determines F_u), so the (u,z) pairs are distinct elements of F. Thus at most |F| nonempty residuals, plus at most one empty residual.

The injection arguments for the third and fourth bounds are valid (distinct patterns have distinct realizing rows by definition).
